## 1. Food truck competition

Chicago's open-data licence file shows 111 distinct vehicle licence accounts, while a city spokesperson count reported in 2025 was 95, so the truck count is a range of about 95 to 111; pizza and Indian trucks are a very small part of it.

- **Truck count and sources.**
  - Open data: 190 active "Mobile Food License" rows, held by 132 distinct accounts (chicago_business_licenses_mobile_food_rows.csv, City of Chicago data portal dataset uupf-x98q, pulled 2026-11-03, A). Every row has status AAI (active) and an expiry date between 2026-11-15 and 2028-10-15, so no closed licences are included. Rows are licences, not trucks, and one business can hold several.
  - By licence activity, the 190 rows split: 115 Mobile Food Preparer (cooks on board), 12 preparer plus previously-prepared food, 1 combined, 10 Mobile Food Dispenser (packaged food), and 52 non-vehicle rows (37 packaged frozen dessert carts, 11 packaged food carts, 4 produce stands) (same file, A). That leaves 138 vehicle licence rows held by 111 distinct accounts (A, my dedupe by account number).
  - City spokesperson: "There are 95 licensed food trucks" (City Cast Chicago, updated 2025-09-30, B). The same page gives 76 trucks in spring 2024, 183 in 2020 and 274 in 2019 (B, a year or more old).
  - Why they differ: the open data counts accounts with any motorized licence (including dispensers and the combined activity) and uses dates up to 2028; the spokesperson's figure may count vehicles or only preparers. Not reconciled. Where to get it: BACP Small Business Center, 312-74-GOBIZ (744-6249).
  - Special Event Food licences are a separate pool: 255 rows, 237 distinct accounts, of which 50 rows are "180 Day Multiple Events - Special Event Food, Mobile Food Vehicle" (A). These are event permits, not additional trucks. Directory counts (Roaming Hunger, Street Food Finder): Not found; the BestFoodTrucks page returned a bot check. Suburban counts: Not found. Where to get it: Cook County Department of Public Health and village clerks.
- **Category breakdown** (my classification of 115 accounts, the 111 vehicle accounts plus 4 produce-stand accounts, by business name only, so approximate and not an official category; C-grade inference on an A-grade list).
  - Tacos and Mexican: about 43 (37%), for example Mexi-Tacos, Delicias Tacos, Los Gorditos.
  - Desserts, coffee, juice and bakery: about 23 (20%), for example Chicago City Ice Cream Express, Kona Ice of Niles.
  - Burgers, BBQ, chicken and American: about 15 (13%), for example Soul & Smoke, Extreme Burger, Roost Chicken & Biscuits.
  - Caribbean: 3, for example Whadda Jerk.
  - Mediterranean, halal and Middle Eastern: 3 (Shawarman Corp., Halal Truck Guys, Yummy Halal Food).
  - Indian or South Asian by name: 2 (Indian Garden, Lahori Bites).
  - Pizza by name: 1 (Da Pizza Dude).
  - Other or unclear name: about 25.
  - East and Southeast Asian: none identifiable by name.
- **Vegetarian, vegan and gluten-free trucks.** None of the licence names clearly centres on these diets. Search results named CheSa's Gluten Free Food Truck (100% gluten-free), Soul Vegetarian / Ste Martaen (vegan), Happy Tummy and The Taco Joint (vegetarian), all C: listings of uncertain age, current licence status not checked. Roaming Hunger tags Da Pizza Dude and Bombay Wraps as Vegetarian (B). Not found: a count. Where to get it: Roaming Hunger and BestFoodTrucks category filters (JavaScript pages).
- **Pizza vendors** (up to 8; searched Roaming Hunger, BestFoodTrucks via search, WeddingWire/Knot listings; the BestFoodTrucks page was blocked, so the list may be short).
  - Da Pizza Dude: Chicago; tomato-based pizzas (Margherita, meatball, mushroom and pepper) listed on Roaming Hunger, 11+ years on the platform, tagged Vegetarian, books through Roaming Hunger (B); a search summary says it accommodates vegan, vegetarian, halal and kosher requests (C). Also in the city licence file under a mobile food licence (A). Prices: Not found.
  - Stix n Brix Pizza: Chicago, "wood-fired taste across the Southside since 2017", drop-off and popup catering rather than a street truck, strengths listed as indoor events, corporate and weddings (B, Roaming Hunger). Prices: Not found.
  - Kissed By Fire BBQ & Pizza Truck, Billy Bricks (all-glass wood-fired trucks, listed near Woodstock), Kurbside Pizza (Lake Zurich) and Popup Chicago (mobile brick ovens): named in search results only (C). Whether they work inside Chicago was not confirmed.
  - No Indian-fusion or tandoor-fired pizza vendor found among these (A/B/C: not found in any source read).
- **Indian and South Asian vendors** (searched Roaming Hunger, search results for Chicago Indian trucks).
  - Spicy Desi Chicago: Indian street food in tacos, bowls and sides (butter chicken taco, paneer tikka taco, samosas, masala fries, mango lassi), a "Vegetarians" strength, 6 months on Roaming Hunger, books through Roaming Hunger (B). It is a fusion format, but nothing on the page shows tandoor cooking, so no claim is made. Prices: Not found on the page.
  - Bombay Wraps: wraps and bowls such as a lamb curry wrap, 7+ years on Roaming Hunger, catering and truck, three past catering bookings of 40 to 60 guests listed in 2020 (B, older than two years).
  - Indian Garden and Lahori Bites appear as active mobile licences in the city file (A); menus and activity were not checked.
  - The Kati Roll, Curry in a Hurry and Curried (2013) appear in older or low-quality results (C, status unknown).
- **Price ranges.** Not found: no truck menu page read showed prices (0 menus sampled with prices). Where to get it: each truck's own site or Instagram, or a phone/menu check.
- **Recurring praise and complaints.** Not found for individual trucks (no ratings or reviews read). Industry-level themes from the sources read: restrictions on parking and location limit when and where trucks can sell, and the 2018 U.S. Chamber of Commerce Foundation report ranked Chicago among the most difficult U.S. cities to run a truck (City Cast page, B, 2018 report older than two years).
- **Common locations and booking channels.** Roaming Hunger is the booking channel for all four profiled trucks (B). Public street spots are limited by the 200-foot and 4-hour rules (see Module 8). Chicago Food Truck Fest runs Fridays in summer at Daley Plaza, per City Cast (B). Logan Square opened a dedicated food truck plaza in summer 2024 (B, via City Cast, citing Eater).
- **Claim limits.** Nothing here shows that any named vendor operates a tandoor on a truck.

Not found: directory truck counts; per-truck prices; ratings and review counts; social following; a count of vegetarian or gluten-free trucks; suburban truck counts. Where to get it: Roaming Hunger and Street Food Finder city pages, each truck's Instagram and Google Maps listing, CCDPH and village licensing records.
